speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly how the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and have you experienced any recent trauma or insect bites to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury is classic for a mallet finger, but I need to assess the extent of the damage. Can you actively straighten the tip of your right ring finger against resistance, and is there any visible deformity or bruising at the nail bed?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The inability to flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint and the extended resting position strongly suggest a flexor digitorum profundus avulsion, commonly known as a Jersey finger, rather than a mallet finger. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_Right_Hand

DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey finger (Flexor digitorum profundus avulsion)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
